name: Itamar (Aaron's son)
title: Aaron's youngest son and priestly ancestor
summary: Itamar was the youngest of Aaron's four sons and served as a priest at the tabernacle. After his older brothers Nadab and Abihu died for offering unauthorized fire before the Lord, Itamar continued to serve faithfully alongside his brother Eleazar. His descendants formed an important priestly lineage in Israel.

keyEvents.title: Consecrated for Priestly Service
keyEvents.description: Itamar, along with his father and brothers, was consecrated for priestly service at the tabernacle as the first priests in Israel.

keyEvents.title: Survived His Brothers' Death
keyEvents.description: When Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord after offering unauthorized fire, Itamar and Eleazar were strictly instructed to continue their duties without mourning publicly.

keyEvents.title: Supervision of the Tabernacle Work
keyEvents.description: Itamar was given responsibility to oversee the work of the Levites at the tabernacle, especially that of the Gershonites and Merarites.

keyEvents.title: Leader of the Levite Families
keyEvents.description: During the wilderness journey, Itamar had oversight of the transport and maintenance of the tabernacle's equipment through the Levite families under his leadership.

keyEvents.title: Ancestor of a Priestly Lineage
keyEvents.description: Itamar's descendants formed one of the two major priestly lines in Israel. The priest Eli and his descendants were descended from Itamar.
